issue_context.title: We need a way to get an event for the routing template
issue_context.body:
Certain tools are looking to for ways to group request by route template (if there is any). We should send that via the `HostingEventSource`.

cc @shirhatti
comments: Can you explain more? Why is route template the right thing?

Moving this out of MVC and out of the backlog 😄 .

The idea is to launch a profiler and run test and bucket requests under the route template. (e.g. `/api/todo/{id}`). Think of this like trying to show all calls to a method (the template) and then having the ability to look at specific requests to dig too (ones with values from the actual URL).

I think it's fine for us to include the route template in an event/log - but it's not the *right thing* because there's a lot more subtlety when you consider realistic apps. I'd suggest that we include the display name of the endpoint and use that as the key. We will have to do some work to make sure we're generating good display names.
How is this hosting? Isn't it Routing that would trigger the event?
I was thinking it would be triggered from the HostingEventSource but that's actually too early.
it should be triggered in the endpoint invoker middleware
Moving to servers since this change would be in Http.Abstractions.

Pre-planning notes: We talked about keeping this in 5.0 because we think the proxy will need it, but given most of our discussions there have been around counters, it feels like the main need here is to put the route template into the counter "scope" to be able to be used as a dimension on which to aggregate counters.
It's not just for counters but for other diagnostics tools.
I know, just trying to prioritize based on our committed work.

I want to work on this issue. I have some questions. 

1. What counters each endpoints need? Right now I have added Request Rate, Total Requests, Current Requests and Failed Requests.

2. What key should be used for endpoints? I have used `DisplayName`, but multiple routes could have the same `DisplayName` and their counters would add up. I could use `RoutePattern` but it's only available on `RouteEndpoint`? What should happened for other type of Endpoints. Although again multiple endpoints could have the same `RouteEndpoint` with different methods.
Waiting for dimensions support in counters, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/26727
@davidfowl Why did you close this issue?
It's unclear if we still need it for the VS tooling.
He's trying to erase me from history

VS tooling aside, I think your original ask is worth solving

> The idea is to launch a profiler and run test and bucket requests under the route template. (e.g. /api/todo/{id}). Think of this like trying to show all calls to a method (the template) and then having the ability to look at specific requests to dig too (ones with values from the actual URL).

review_comments: Nit: one empty line too much.

May it be "better" to handle the _executed_ within the _failed_?
So that here is just one method call, and in the internals of `Log.FailedEndpoint` this case gets handled and has the potential to adapt it later if needed.

Looking up a dictionary multiple times (executing, executed, failed) for every call would have a performance impact. This code is on a very hot path.

I don't know the best way to mitigate but EventSource.OnEventCommand provides a hook to decide to enable counters. We should only be initializing counters when needed.

The problem is that even if the event source is disabled, we would still need to do the dictionary lookup to ensure `EndpointCounter._totalRequests/_currentRequests/_failedRequests` are all accurate when the event source becomes enabled.

We can still override OnEventCommand to lazily initialize the PollingCounters, but we'd have to iterate `_endpointCounters` dictionary when the event source becomes enabled to do so.
Ah, right. We could add counters as metadata or a property on the endpoint. However endpoints are intended to be immutable and Ryan would murder us all 😄

I was thinking the same thing. Problem with a property is that Endpoint is defined in another assembly and InternalsVisibleTo is bad. Putting it in Metadata doesn't work because it *is* immutable and Ryan would murder us. Retrieving the EndpointCounter from Metadata would involve a dictionary lookup anyway.

Another option is to have the routing matcher store the counter, and matching an endpoint would return endpoint+counter tulple.

Would need to store it somewhere until endpoint invocation.
Or have a setting enabling per-endpoint counters. By default they are off, and if you value the counters over the the perf loss then you'd set a flag on `RouteOptions`.

> Another option is to have the routing matcher store the counter, and matching an endpoint would return endpoint+counter tulple.

That seems interesting. Would we create a new internal feature interface just for storing the counter?

Yes.

There would be some other challenges, like an application's endpoints can change. For example, dropping a new Razor file into a directory would change that endpoint data source to include the new endpoint and the matcher would recompute the DFA graph. When that happens we'd need to keep the endpoint+counter instances together. Not difficult, but something to take into account.

What should happen if someone wants to [`SetEndpoint`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/f45250ce5e423dad083fe99967a4d65782c5301e/src/Http/Http.Abstractions/src/Routing/EndpointHttpContextExtensions.cs#L34) without Routing Middleware. Do they need to provide the counter data as well?

Correct me if I'm wrong,  but Routing matcher only gives `RouteEndpoint` not `Endpoint`, and If we are going with  getting counters from Routing matcher, can we instead add a property to `RouteEndpoint` and since it's in the same assembly as there's no need to `InternalVisibleTo`.

Routing matching usual matches `RouteEndpoint` but can return `Endpoint` from a policy.

That's a good point about SetEndpoint. Matching is the primary way of setting endpoints, but not the only way. Matching providing the counter type wouldn't work.
@noahfalk This is an example of where we want dimensions for metrics to avoid the dictionary workaround.
